source.title: Polygonal Unadjusted Langevin Algorithms: Creating stable and efficient adaptive algorithms for neural networks

record.tranche_reason: Compares optimizer test performance on image and language tasks, bearing on whether adaptive methods generalize worse than SGD; it does not test training error or random-label memorization.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Wilson et al. for an adaptive-optimizer generalization finding; that cited result is not this study's evidence. Its own optimizer comparisons report test accuracy or perplexity, but no training performance. Table 2 values are assigned using its optimizer and model headings.
record.test_reason: The study's own image-classification comparisons measure Adam and other adaptive optimizers against momentum SGD. Its language experiments compare AdaBelief with averaged SGD. These results bear on V4, including its broader-tuning qualification, although the limited-tuning protocol and training-performance comparison are not reproduced.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate: the authors conclude that TheoPouLa combines stability and convergence guarantees with superior empirical performance on their tested image and language tasks. They attribute its generalization partly to a transition from adaptive updates toward SGD-like updates. That attribution is their proposed explanation; the experiments do not isolate the transition as the cause.
record.recipe_differences: Compares optimizers on CIFAR image classification and Penn Treebank language modeling; it does not reproduce the original study's benchmark suite or limited-tuning protocol.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer comparisons vary by model, dataset, and task. For TheoPouLa, the paper also reports test accuracy changes with learning rate, boosting parameter ε, and inverse temperature β.

fits_no_version.finding: TheoPouLa's superiority over comparator optimizers, its hyperparameter sensitivity, and its boosting-function and regularization ablations evaluate the proposed method. Its toy example and convergence theorems concern optimization and stability.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: TheoPouLa can improve held-out performance and optimization stability through its taming, boosting and Langevin updates.

record.problems: The optimizer comparisons report test metrics but no training performance, so the training-versus-test relationship in V4 cannot be assessed. The experiments use a selected hyperparameter search, and only three runs are reported for the image and language experiments.

untested.parts: Fitting random labels and comparing held-out performance under random and natural labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

The protocol tuning only learning rates and decay schedules; equal or better training performance accompanying worse held-out performance; decoupled weight decay; and direct Adam-versus-SGD comparisons on word-level language modeling. Language experiments do compare AdaBelief with averaged SGD.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that compensate for larger batches.
Controlled dropout comparisons, including dataset-size and augmentation interactions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, generalization-gap correlations, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Removing memorized examples versus randomly selected examples and retraining.

missing.what: Add other adaptive-optimizer comparisons against SGD from Table 2. In task order CIFAR-10 VGG/ResNet/DenseNet, then CIFAR-100 VGG/ResNet/DenseNet: AdaBelief accuracies are 92.17/95.29/95.58/69.50/77.33/79.12; AdamP 91.68/95.18/95.17/69.41/76.14/77.58; AdaBound 91.81/94.83/95.05/68.61/76.27/77.56; AMSGrad 91.24/93.76/93.74/67.71/73.51/74.50; RMSProp 90.82/93.06/92.89/65.45/71.79/71.75. SGD baselines are 90.73/94.61/94.46/67.78/77.16/78.95. Preserve the reported standard deviations. These comparisons show that deficits depend on optimizer as well as architecture.

Add SWATS comparisons with Adam and SGD to assess the switching qualification. SWATS accuracies are 87.29 (4.210), 94.76 (0.565), 95.04 (0.339) on CIFAR-10 VGG/ResNet/DenseNet; CIFAR-100 has no VGG result, 73.86 (3.928) for ResNet and 78.81 (1.812) for DenseNet. Recovery is architecture-dependent, with substantial variability in some settings.

Add AdaBelief versus NT-ASGD language comparisons. Test perplexity for one/two/three layers is 84.46 (0.272)/67.34 (0.496)/61.52 (0.302) for AdaBelief and 82.85 (0.308)/67.53 (0.171)/61.60 (0.094) for ASGD. Training uses 750 epochs, batch size 20 and gradient clipping 0.25. AdaBelief uses selected learning rates, epsilon and development-based decay; ASGD uses constant learning rates and triggered averaging. The text calls two- and three-layer performance comparable.

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 values in R1–R12 are correctly assigned. States must follow the direction of V4, so Adam performing worse is observed, not reversed. Reciprocal Adam/SGD rows duplicate each comparison. Image results are means and standard deviations of best test accuracy over three runs, rather than a reported validation-selected final-checkpoint comparison. Broader tuning is tested without a limited-versus-broader tuning ablation, so its causal role cannot be inferred. The study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Training performance; language benchmarks comparing Adam directly with SGD; the claim's limited-tuning condition, since the paper uses extensive hyperparameter search.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other generalization measures.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated 2 March 2024. Image results are means and standard deviations across three runs of best test accuracy; reciprocal rows are not independent evidence, and no significance test establishes the small VGG differences. Only the Langevin architecture-specific switching claim in the synthesis statement concerns this study.
